questions.question: What does a graded relevance label represent?
options: A level of result usefulness rather than only relevant or irrelevant
The number of tokens in a result
The document's position before ranking
The time required to build the index

questions.question: Why does DCG discount results at later ranks?
options: Later results always have lower relevance labels
User attention and utility generally decline with rank
Discounting makes every query binary
The ideal ranking contains no later results

questions.question: Using exponential gain, what gain is assigned to relevance grade 2?

options: DCG after reversing the returned list
The average DCG over all queries
DCG calculated with binary labels only
The greatest DCG@k attainable by ideally ordering judged results

questions.question: Observed DCG@3 is 7.2 and IDCG@3 is 9.0. What is nDCG@3?

options: New rankers cannot return graded results
Novel relevant documents may not have been included in the original judgment pool
IDCG must always equal zero for a new ranker
Discounting is disabled for unjudged documents
